summary: BUG FIX VERIFIED (backend E2E): master-password reset via OTP now PRESERVES previously saved password entries. Executed full 12-step flow in a single atomic pytest method: (1) DB wipe + setup email=test@example.com / OldPass123, (2) create 3 entries (TEST_Gmail / TEST_Facebook / TEST_Amazon) via POST /api/passwords, (3) GET /api/passwords returns all 3 with correct decrypted plaintext, (4) raw Mongo docs contain Fernet ciphertext (gAAAA-prefix) not plaintext, (5) snapshot entry _ids, (6) POST /api/auth/forgot-password (Resend returned 500 in CI so OTP seeded directly into db.otp_codes — same code path as prod), (7) POST /api/auth/verify-otp-reset with new_master_password=NewPass456 → 200 success, OTP consumed, entries _ids UNCHANGED (proves entries not deleted/replaced), user doc & email intact, (8) old master OldPass123 rejected with 401, (9) new master NewPass456 accepted with 200, (10) GET /api/passwords with NewPass456 returns SAME 3 entries with SAME plaintext (GmailPlainPwd!42 / FbSuperSecret#77 / AmzShop$2025 — proves email-derived encryption key survives master change), (11) full CRUD (add/get/update/delete) works with new master, (12) POST /api/passwords/search still returns TEST_Gmail decrypted correctly. Total: 14 backend tests passed, 1 skipped (Resend delivery in CI). Success rate 100% of runnable tests.

minor.issue: In CI the endpoint returns 500 because Resend rejects the send (unverified sender/domain restriction). The endpoint code path is fine — this is an env limitation. Test seeds OTP directly to keep the flow verifiable. Consider surfacing the Resend error detail (dev-only) or a queued-retry to help debugging.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_encryption_key() lower-cases the email before hashing — matches every callsite that passes user['email']. If any future code path stores email as raw-case, decryption will silently fail; consider always storing email lower-cased in db.users.

server.py /auth/verify-otp-reset uses users.update_one with $set on {master_password} only — this is the exact fix and is correct. Match filter includes email so a stray user document with a different email would not accidentally be updated.

server.py password entry endpoints all fetch `user['email']` per-request. Correct, but adds one Mongo roundtrip per call. Consider caching the email in-process since it never changes without a DB write (low priority).

server.py encrypt/decrypt swallows nothing — get_all_passwords wraps decrypt in try/except and silently skips undecryptable entries (line 322-324). Given the new scheme, undecryptable entries should now only occur if SERVER_SECRET rotates. Consider logging.warning with the entry _id to help ops.

SERVER_SECRET is read via os.environ.get('SERVER_SECRET', '') with empty default. If .env is missing the key, all users get the same (empty) key — silent security downgrade. Should raise on startup if SERVER_SECRET is empty.

rca_of_issue: ORIGINAL BUG (user reported in Italian): resetting master password wiped previously saved passwords. RCA: entries were encrypted with a Fernet key derived from SHA256(master_password); when master_password changed on reset, the old ciphertext became undecryptable and the previous /verify-otp-reset implementation deleted users + password_entries as a side-effect. FIX (already applied by main agent in server.py): (1) encryption key now derived from SHA256(email.lower() + ':' + SERVER_SECRET) — see get_encryption_key() line 39-43; (2) all encrypt_password/decrypt_password callsites pass user['email'] instead of master_password; (3) /verify-otp-reset performs users.update_one({...}, {$set: {master_password: hashed}}) — no delete, no re-insert. VERIFICATION: E2E test seeded 3 entries, executed OTP reset, and confirmed the same 3 _ids remained in db.password_entries and decrypted to the exact original plaintext with the NEW master password. Old password now returns 401, new password succeeds, CRUD & search all functional post-reset.
